import os import pandas as pd import numpy as np from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer import lightgbm as lgb import warnings warnings.filterwarnings("ignore") # Configuration INPUT_DIR = "./input" SUBMISSION_DIR = "./submission" TARGET_COLS = ["toxic", "severe_toxic", "obscene", "threat", "insult", "identity_hate"] # Create submission directory if it doesn't exist os.makedirs(SUBMISSION_DIR, exist_ok=True) # Load data train_df = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(INPUT_DIR, "train.csv")) test_df = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(INPUT_DIR, "test.csv")) # Preprocessing function def preprocess_text(text): if pd.isna(text): return "" text = str(text).lower() text = text.replace("
", " ") text = text.replace(" ", " ") text = text.replace("<", " ") text = text.replace(">", " ") text = text.replace("\t", " ") text = text.strip() return text # Apply preprocessing train_df["clean_text"] = train_df["comment_text"].apply(preprocess_text) test_df["clean_text"] = test_df["comment_text"].apply(preprocess_text) # Train-Validation Split (80/20) # Ensures a hold-out set that the model never sees during training train_subset, val_subset = train_test_split( train_df, test_size=0.2, random_state=42, shuffle=True ) # Feature Vectorization with TF-IDF vectorizer = TfidfVectorizer( max_features=10000, ngram_range=(1, 2), min_df=2, max_df=0.95, sublinear_tf=True ) # Transform text features X_train = vectorizer.fit_transform(train_subset["clean_text"]) X_val = vectorizer.transform(val_subset["clean_text"]) X_test = vectorizer.transform(test_df["clean_text"]) # Initialize submission dataframe submission_data = test_df[["id"]].copy() # List to store validation AUC scores validation_aucs = [] # Train models for each target for col in TARGET_COLS: # Extract target labels y_train = train_subset[col].astype(int) y_val = val_subset[col].astype(int) # Train LightGBM model model = lgb.LGBMClassifier( n_estimators=300, learning_rate=0.05, num_leaves=31, subsample=0.8, colsample_bytree=0.8, reg_alpha=0.1, reg_lambda=0.1, min_child_samples=5, random_state=42, verbose=-1, ) # Fit on training subset only (Hold-out validation logic) model.fit(X_train, y_train) # Predict on validation subset val_pred = model.predict_proba(X_val)[:, 1] # Calculate ROC AUC for this column try: auc = roc_auc_score(y_val, val_pred) validation_aucs.append(auc) print(f"Validation AUC for {col}: {auc:.5f}") except Exception as e: print(f"Warning: Could not compute AUC for {col}: {e}") auc = 0.5 validation_aucs.append(0.5) # Predict on test set test_pred = model.predict_proba(X_test)[:, 1] submission_data[col] = test_pred # Calculate Mean Column-wise ROC AUC mean_auc = np.mean(validation_aucs) print(f"Mean Column-wise ROC AUC: {mean_auc:.5f}") # Save submission to the required path submission_data.to_csv(os.path.join(SUBMISSION_DIR, "submission.csv"), index=False) print(f"Submission saved to {SUBMISSION_DIR}/submission.csv")
plan: We will build a text classification solution using LightGBM and TF-IDF features to detect toxicity levels. First, we preprocess the comment text by cleaning HTML tags and normalizing case. We then create a hold-out validation split from the training data (80/20) to ensure an unbiased evaluation metric. For each of the six toxicity labels, we train a separate LightGBM classifier on the training split and evaluate it on the validation set using column-wise ROC AUC, printing the mean score. Finally, we generate predictions for the test set using the same models and save them to the required submission file.
